<tool_use:email>
to: "a.marsh@gmail.com"
subject: "Re: Cedar Creek - latest?"
body: "Hello,

Happy to give you the current, straight picture — there's a lot circulating right now, so I understand the confusion.

Phase 1 (downtown reach): Complete since October 2024. Channel widening and the Harmon St retention basin are performing as designed — the downtown reach is now rated for a 25-year flood event, and minor-flood events at the downtown gauge are down about 60% since completion.

Phase 2 (Willow Glen/Fairmont): This is the phase that would directly protect your area — levee setbacks and storm-drain trunk upgrades. Construction has not started yet. Easement acquisition is at 4 of 11 parcels closed. Our engineering staff's current projection has this phase completing in February 2028, roughly 14 months behind the original schedule.

Budget: the project is currently projected at $38.7M against a $34.5M bond authorization - about 12% over.

You may have seen more optimistic statements - the contractor (Merrick Civil) has proposed an accelerated fall 2027 completion, and there's been public speculation about finishing before the 2027 storm season. I want to be transparent that our county engineer's assessment is that this acceleration is high-risk and not achievable without additional funded crews the current budget doesn't cover. We're treating February 2028 as the realistic planning date, not the more optimistic figures.

In the meantime, the sandbag distribution program remains active at three depots in the district - let me know if you'd like locations and hours. The last two winters have been well below normal rainfall, which has helped, but that's not something to rely on, so it's worth staying prepared.

Let me know if you have other questions or want more detail on any piece of this.

Sincerely,
Constituent Services
Office of Supervisor Dana Reyes, District 3"
</tool_use:email>
